name: Pakistan's Pride and Gairdner Recipient Dr Zulfiqar Bhutta comes to AKU

content.text: In a lecture titled "The Future of Maternal and Child Health: What Does it Mean for the World and Pakistan", Dr Bhutta spoke of his pursuit of improving child and maternal health in the developing world during which he lovingly paid homage to his wife and work companion, Dr Shireen Bhutta who passed away earlier this year.

The lecture celebrated Dr Bhutta's outstanding achievements in healthcare; he is the first Pakistani to win the Gairdner Global Health Award. The Gairdner Awards are among the world's most prestigious scientific honours. Dr Bhutta is the first dual recipient of the AKU Distinguished Faculty Award for Research and AKU Award of Distinction. His accolades include the Global Paediatric Research Award for Outstanding Contributions to Global Child Health, the WHO Ihsan Dogramaci Family Health award and the inaugural TUBA Academy of Sciences Award for global contributions to Health and Life Sciences. Dr Bhutta was admitted to the National Academy of Medicine, the highest academic and scientific platform in North America and has been elected as a Fellow of the Royal Society, the oldest science body in the UK.

During the lecture, Dr Bhutta, who holds the Robert Harding Inaugural Chair in Global Child Health at the Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto and is Co-Director of the SickKids Centre for Global Child Health, remarked that no award or accolade can be won without collaborations and collective efforts. He expressed his gratitude to his students, fellow doctors and mentors, many of whom were part of the audience.

Dr Bhutta's work has been recognized with prestigious awards, honours and grants, globally. These achievements testify not only to the unique talents of Dr Bhutta but also to the enabling environment AKU has created for the development of leaders and change makers. He has also been ranked among the top 100 medicine scientists in the first edition of top scientists ranking for medicine. Having begun his career at AKU in 1986, the institution provided a foundation for the development of an illustrious career in which he built research programmes on maternal and child health and nutrition with national and global impact.
Dr Bhutta, we are proud to have been part of your inspirational journey.

content.title: Pakistan's Pride and Gairdner Recipient Dr Zulfiqar Bhutta comes to AKU
content.author: Fatima Zehra Awan
content.description: A rush of nostalgia and feelings of gratitude were conjured at Aga Khan University (AKU) when Dr Zulfiqar Bhutta, recipient of the John Dirks Gairdner Global Health Award shared the stage with Dr John Dirks himself. AKU has played a key role in both these distinguished doctors' journeys; Dr Dirks is the former Dean of AKU's Faculty of Health Sciences while Dr Bhutta is the Founding Director of the Institute for Global Health and Development and the Centre of Excellence in Women and Child Health at the Aga Khan University.
